title: bug: agent Git guard fails closed when moe-agent.ps1 runs under PowerShell 7, because its powershell.exe Set-Acl child inherits pwsh's PSModulePath and cannot load Get-Acl
description: Repro: native Windows (pwsh 7, Git 2.54, node 24.16). In a git-archive snapshot of 04a3e180, `npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts` fails 'lands once, crashes before the receipt…': the pwsh wrapper stops with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED. It fails the same way on HEAD's own bytes. Surfacing the swallowed error shows the guard program's ACL step (moe-agent.ps1, `cp.spawnSync('powershell.exe', … Get-Acl/Set-Acl)`) exiting 1 with "The 'Get-Acl' command was found in the module 'Microsoft.PowerShell.Security', but the module could not be loaded". That is the known PS7→PS5.1 PSModulePath inheritance. Candidate fix: drop PSModulePath from that child's env. Check the sh twin and the other powershell.exe spawns too. Found by task-f33bf7af's Windows gate.

implementationPlan.description:

First read mem:task-task-44b817f973374dffb578308278050497-handoff (it holds the architect's measured prototype diff), mem:gotcha-pwsh7-agent-git-guard-psmodulepath and mem:gotcha-agent-git-guard-runtime-config.

Preconditions:

Edits (the architect's prototype measured exactly these):
(a) `clean`: add `PSMODULEPATH$` to the stripped-name regex, giving `/^(MOE_|FAKE_|GIT_|CLAUDE|CODEX|GUARD_|PSMODULEPATH$)/i`.
- Why: the fake CLI's own `secure` check spawns powershell.exe for Get-Acl, and under any pwsh ancestor that check fails too (measured: exit 1, CouldNotAutoloadMatchingModule).
- It cannot mask the bug, because pwsh re-adds its own paths at startup.
(b) After `const win = ...`, add `const pwsh = win && spawnSync('pwsh.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-Command', 'exit 0'], { timeout: 60000 }).status === 0;`.
(c) launch(): make the first line `const shell = win ? f.engine || 'powershell.exe' : 'bash';`. Use `shell` in both the concurrent execFile call and the final run call.
(d) CLI matrix:
- Destructure an optional 5th tuple element `opts = {}`.
- Append, on win32 only, `['custom', false, false, 'REVIEW', { engine: 'pwsh.exe' }]`.
- Title prefix: `opts.engine ? 'PS7' : win ? 'PS5.1' : 'bash'`.
- Test options: `{ skip: opts.engine && !pwsh && 'pwsh.exe not found' }`.
- Fixture: `Object.assign(fixture(t, cli, hooks, status), opts)`.
- The body and every assertion stay as they are, and they apply to the PS7 row.
- Why an object: task-76ae5c47 and task-408a0ac1, later in the lane, add their planned `mode` key to it instead of a 6th position.
(e) In that body's first assertion message ('CLI did not run'), take codes from both streams: `(r.stdout + r.stderr).match(/MOE_[A-Z_]+/g)` instead of `r.stdout?.match(...)`. The ps1 throw goes to stderr, so HEAD prints codes=null. A RED run now names MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED.
(f) In the `if (process.argv[2] !== 'cli') {` block, add the test 'both wrappers embed one guard program, and it keeps PSModulePath from its powershell.exe child'.
- Cut moe-agent.sh between `<<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'\n` and `\nMOE_GIT_GUARD_JS\n`.
- Cut moe-agent.ps1 between `$program = @'\n` and `\n'@\n`.
- Assert that each opening anchor occurs exactly once, and that the two programs are equal.
- Assert that the program matches /'PSMODULEPATH'/. That is the quoted code literal, so the comment alone cannot satisfy it.
- This is the only check of the sh twin: Linux never takes the win32 branch, and parity-check.sh does not compare the programs.

RED proof. Record both lines in the step note.
- Snapshot: `git archive HEAD scripts docs` into `mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/g44b8-red-XXXX`, plus only this file.
- Linux: `node --test --test-name-pattern='embed one guard program' scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs` gives 1 fail.
- Windows, with cwd in that /mnt/d snapshot (a UNC cwd breaks node --test): `"/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^PS7 ' scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs` gives `not ok 1 - PS7 custom headless plumbing completion ...` with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED among its codes.
- Then delete the snapshot.
The architect saw both RED on HEAD 09120533. Expected counts after steps 2-3: Linux 25 tests, Windows 26.

GREEN, scripts/moe-agent.ps1: function Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard, the `$program = @'...'@` here-string, inside the `if (win) {` block. Any editor works (Edit, apply_patch), as long as the file keeps its UTF-8 BOM (first bytes ef bb bf) and LF-only endings; parity-check.sh enforces the BOM. Never rewrite it through a shell pipeline.
Replace the one line
`        value(cp.spawnSync('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-EncodedCommand', Buffer.from(acl, 'utf16le').toString('base64')], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 10000, maxBuffer: 1048576 }));`
with these three (8-space indent):
`        // pwsh 7 lists its own modules first in PSModulePath, and a Windows PowerShell 5.1 child that inherits it cannot load Get-Acl.`
`        const psenv = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k]) => k.toUpperCase() !== 'PSMODULEPATH'));`
`        value(cp.spawnSync('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-EncodedCommand', Buffer.from(acl, 'utf16le').toString('base64')], { env: psenv, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 10000, maxBuffer: 1048576 }));`
Why this shape (each point is measured or sourced in the handoff memory):
- Without the variable, 5.1 builds its own default module path. pwsh repairs PSModulePath only for a powershell.exe it starts directly, never for a grandchild started through node.
- libuv's Windows env injection does not list PSModulePath, so the drop holds (mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-env-injection).
- Compare keys case-insensitively, because a spread process.env is no longer case-insensitive (the lowercase-count lesson).
- Start from process.env, not the program's `env` const, so the child keeps exactly its old environment minus that one variable.
Error handling is unchanged. A non-zero exit, timeout or spawn error of the ACL child still throws in value(); the catch removes the root, and the wrapper stops with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED (fail closed).
Leave untouched:
- the `& node -` line;
- Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand and Remove-MoeAgentGitGuard, whose span the launcher harnesses cut;
- every launch line, which codexDescriptor.ts pins;
- the rest of the program.
Check: the step-1 PS7 row passes on native Windows from a fresh /mnt/d snapshot with this file overlaid. The twin test stays red until step 3.

GREEN, scripts/moe-agent.sh: function prepare_agent_git_guard, the `<<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'` heredoc. Make the same three-line replacement as step 2, byte-identical. The delimiter is quoted, so bash expands nothing in the JS.
Live seats execute this file, and bash parses launch code above the main loop incrementally, so never rewrite it in place (scripts/CLAUDE.md, Hot reload):
1. `T=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/g44b8-sh-XXXX) && cp -p scripts/moe-agent.sh "$T/moe-agent.sh"`. This is the same D: volume, so the mv below is a rename.
2. Edit "$T/moe-agent.sh" with any editor.
3. Run `bash -n "$T/moe-agent.sh"`. Then `grep -c $'\r' "$T/moe-agent.sh"` must print 0.
4. `mv -f "$T/moe-agent.sh" scripts/moe-agent.sh && rmdir "$T"`.
5. `git diff --stat -- scripts/moe-agent.sh` shows +3/-1 and no mode change.
Then the step-1 twin test passes: `node --test --test-name-pattern='embed one guard program' scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs`. That name-filtered run only reads the two wrappers, so it may run in place.
Error handling: nothing new. prepare_agent_git_guard's caller already turns a failed program into MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED and exit 1.

VERIFY ONCE, after steps 1-3. Fresh output of this exact command is the complete_task evidence. Run it from the repo root on this WSL seat, in the background, and wait for VERIFY_EXIT. It takes about 25-30 min: the guard suite about 1 min on Linux and 2.5 min on Windows, acceptance 20 s, pwsh postflight about 20 min.

What it proves:

executionContract.intendedBehavior: On Windows, the agent Git guard's ACL step runs without an inherited PSModulePath. That step is the powershell.exe Get-Acl/Set-Acl child spawned by the embedded node program in moe-agent.ps1 (Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard) and in moe-agent.sh (prepare_agent_git_guard). A wrapper started under PowerShell 7, or anywhere below a pwsh ancestor (for example a pwsh CI step running node, which runs the 5.1 wrapper), therefore sets up the guard and launches its CLI instead of failing closed with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED. PS 5.1 seats and Linux/macOS behave exactly as before.
acceptanceCriteria: agent-git-guard.test.mjs gains a win32-only row 'PS7 custom headless plumbing completion ...' that runs moe-agent.ps1 under pwsh.exe with every PS5.1-row assertion. It is RED against HEAD's wrappers, passes with the fix, and is not skipped on the gate host.
A twin test asserts that both wrappers embed the same program and that it carries the 'PSMODULEPATH' filter. It is RED on HEAD.
Every existing guard row passes on Linux (bash) and on native Windows (PS 5.1), and parity-check.sh passes.

The description's repro, delivery/acceptance.test.ts 'lands once, crashes before the receipt...', passes natively under pwsh 7. postflight.ps1 under pwsh 7 reports failureClass NONE (the governor's request).
invariants: The embedded guard program stays byte-identical between moe-agent.sh's MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS heredoc and moe-agent.ps1's $program here-string, and a test enforces it.
A failing ACL child (non-zero exit, timeout or spawn error) still fails closed: MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED, the temp root removed, no CLI launch.
Only PSModulePath (in any letter case) leaves that one child's environment. Every other variable is inherited as before, and the git spawns' env is unchanged.

moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM and LF endings. moe-agent.sh is replaced by a validated rename (bash -n), never rewritten in place. No byte changes in any launch line, the `& node -` line, Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand or Remove-MoeAgentGitGuard.
compatibility: No MCP tool, wire or .moe state change. Seats the JetBrains plugin launches under PS 5.1 behave exactly as before.
The later guard rows task-76ae5c47 and task-408a0ac1 can add a `mode` key to the new matrix options object.

In scripts/moe-agent.sh, prepare_agent_git_guard's `<<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'` heredoc holds the same 56-line program, byte-identical at 09120533.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen: drop PSModulePath (any letter case) from the guard program's powershell.exe ACL child only, as the description proposes. Measured natively: HEAD's program exits 1 under pwsh 7.6.9, the patched one exits 0, and both exit 0 under PS 5.1. Rejected: (1) replacing Get-Acl/Set-Acl with [IO.Directory]::GetAccessControl/SetAccessControl. It is module-free and also measured working, but it rewrites the reviewed ACL code, and the env fix also covers any future cmdlet in that child. (2) Stripping PSModulePath before launching pwsh: pwsh re-adds its own paths at startup (mem:gotcha-pwsh7-agent-git-guard-psmodulepath). (3) Rebuilding a 5.1 value the way pwsh does for a direct child: more code, and 5.1 builds the same default itself when the variable is absent. (4) A full PS7 matrix of 11 rows: it doubles Windows runtime, and guard setup is the only engine-dependent code, so one full-assertion row suffices. (5) Changing the other powershell.exe callers: measured unaffected (see codebaseInsights).
